scope: Domain lifecycle: spec domain new / spec domain list and charter editing. Belongs here: the born-valid scaffold (spec domain new); the domain list output; the scope charter field on the envelope. Does not belong here: requirement authoring (spec req/supersede/amend → REQ). Boundary case: minting a requirement id is REQ, scaffolding the domain that holds it is DOMAIN.

requirements.statement: Domain-name input is normalized before validation — uppercase plus strip ALL whitespace; spaces are never converted to dashes.
requirements.why: A dash is HEAD_RE's key/seq separator; a dashed key scaffolds a spec that silently parses to zero requirements.

requirements.statement: spec domain new prints exactly one `<raw>` → <KEY> transformation line when uppercasing the name and stripping its whitespace changed the input, and prints no such line when the input was already a canonical key.
requirements.why: The author must be able to see the silent transformation applied on their behalf; hiding it lets a surprising key scaffold a domain the author never intended to name.

requirements.statement: The post-normalization key must match KEY_RE /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$/; failure prints to stderr and exits 2.
requirements.why: Only KEY_RE-clean keys produce headings the parser can bind.

requirements.statement: spec domain new <KEY> creates spec-engine/<KEY>/SPEC.json as a complete, valid domain envelope — key, owner null, specVersion 1, and the current date in the author's local timezone — so spec index ingests the new domain immediately with zero diagnostics.
requirements.why: A scaffold must be born valid: a file the indexer cannot parse yields a domain with zero requirements and no error, and a UTC-computed date stamps evening authors with tomorrow.

requirements.statement: spec domain new <KEY> refuses to overwrite an existing spec-engine/<KEY>/SPEC.json — it prints an error to stderr and exits 2.
The resolved scaffold destination must stay inside the platform directory; violation exits 2.
requirements.why: Path-containment defense in depth even though KEY_RE already blocks traversal characters.

requirements.statement: A domain is a child directory of spec-engine/ containing a SPEC.json, enumerated from the filesystem — never from the derived index or a cache file.
requirements.why: Canonical truth is the git spec location; a second derived store would violate the derived-DB constraint.

requirements.statement: spec domain list prints the keys sorted lexicographically, one per line, exit 0; zero domains produce empty output and still exit 0.
requirements.why: Authors need to see what exists; prefix resolution builds on this listing.

requirements.statement: spec domain list on a missing or non-directory spec-engine/ prints the friendly not-a-platform message and exits 2.

spec domain new <KEY> creates spec-engine/<KEY>/SPEC.json as a complete, valid domain envelope — key, owner null, the current date in the author's local timezone, and no authored specVersion for a requirement domain (only the reserved TERM domain is seeded with specVersion 1) — so spec index ingests the new domain immediately with zero diagnostics.
requirements.why: A scaffold must be born valid: a file the indexer cannot parse yields a domain with zero requirements and no error, and a UTC-computed date stamps evening authors with tomorrow; seeding an authored specVersion on a requirement domain would plant a second version counter beside the derived one, free to drift from the supersede history.

requirements.statement: When spec domain new receives a name, it shall normalize it before validation — uppercase plus strip all whitespace — and shall never convert spaces to dashes.
requirements.why: A dash is the key/sequence separator in requirement ids; a dashed key scaffolds a domain whose entries silently parse to zero requirements.

requirements.statement: When normalization changed the input name, spec domain new shall print exactly one <raw> → <KEY> transformation line, and shall print no such line when the input was already canonical.
requirements.why: The author must see the silent transformation applied on their behalf; hiding it lets a surprising key scaffold a domain the author never intended to name.

requirements.statement: If the normalized domain key does not match /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$/, then spec domain new shall print an error to stderr and exit 2.
requirements.why: A key outside that grammar produces an envelope the shared domain schema rejects, so the scaffolded domain would index to zero requirements with no error.

requirements.statement: If spec-engine/<KEY>/SPEC.json already exists, then spec domain new shall refuse to overwrite it, printing an error to stderr and exiting 2.
requirements.why: Overwriting would reset an authored domain to an empty scaffold, destroying every requirement it held — canonical-truth loss in the file git treats as the source.

requirements.statement: If the resolved destination of spec domain new's scaffold falls outside the platform directory, then the command shall refuse the write and exit 2.
requirements.why: Without this containment check, a regression in key normalization or validation could let a crafted name write a scaffold outside the platform tree.

requirements.statement: When enumerating domains, the engine shall treat each child directory of spec-engine/ containing a SPEC.json as a domain, reading the filesystem only — never the derived index or a cache file.
requirements.why: Canonical truth is the git spec location; a second derived store would let the domain listing drift from what actually exists on disk.

requirements.statement: When spec domain list runs, it shall print the domain keys sorted lexicographically, one per line, and exit 0 — zero domains shall produce empty output and still exit 0.
requirements.why: Prefix resolution and scripted listings build on this output; an unstable order or an error exit on an empty platform would break both.

requirements.statement: If spec domain list runs where spec-engine/ is missing or not a directory, then it shall print the friendly not-a-platform message and exit 2.
requirements.why: A raw throw at the boundary buries the fix; the guidance-plus-exit-2 contract keeps the failure actionable and lets scripts branch on the usage code.

requirements.statement: When spec domain new <KEY> scaffolds, it shall write spec-engine/<KEY>/SPEC.json as a complete valid envelope — key, owner null, the current local-timezone date, and no authored specVersion for a requirement domain (only the reserved TERM domain seeds specVersion 1) — so spec index ingests it immediately with zero diagnostics.
requirements.why: A scaffold the indexer cannot parse yields a domain with zero requirements and no error; a UTC date stamps evening authors with tomorrow; and an authored specVersion on a requirement domain plants a second version counter free to drift from the derived one.
